members.position: THEORY: Ship Claude account brokering first as an optional, external broker integration that uses T3's existing per-instance environment and secret-store seams, rather than embedding aigate-specific behavior in the core provider. THEORY: Represent Muse and Kimi as explicitly configured Claude-compatible route profiles, not as models discovered from aigate; defer account hopping within a live T3 session until the Agent SDK and credential-isolation experiments pass. THEORY: Keep Codex, Cursor, Grok, and OpenCode unchanged in v1, while defining generic broker contracts so later providers can opt in without provider-specific assumptions.

claims.claim: VERIFIED: T3 can inject sensitive, per-provider-instance environment variables and isolate Claude configuration directories.
claims.evidence: apps/server/src/provider/ProviderInstanceEnvironment.ts:3-16; Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts:128; packages/contracts/src/providerInstance.ts:104-113; serverSettings.ts:316-376; Drivers/ClaudeHome.ts:27-33; the brief also reports an existing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY test.

claims.claim: VERIFIED: aigate selects the account with the lowest max(5-hour usage, 7-day usage) among eligible accounts and exposes selection, usage, limit-event, and provider-key APIs, but exposes no model-listing endpoint.
claims.evidence: Operator-researched aigate src/server.js:295-298; measured GET /api/accounts and GET /api/select; listed API inventory; README/COMPLIANCE.md.

claims.claim: THEORY: A first release should call aigate at process/session start and inject the selected Claude OAuth token, rather than attempting per-turn account switching.
claims.evidence: The existing aigate-run.sh rotates by launching a new process and resumes interactive work with --continue, while T3 uses the Agent SDK query/session path in Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:4154-4192 and ProviderService.startSession/sendTurn.
claims.test: Run a controlled T3 session against two disposable Claude accounts, exhaust or synthetically trigger the first account's quota, then verify whether a new query can resume the same thread on the second account without lost context, duplicated tool effects, or protocol corruption.

claims.claim: CONTESTED: Environment-injected Claude OAuth credentials may or may not override a stored macOS Keychain login when T3 uses the Agent SDK and an instance-specific CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.
claims.evidence: aigate-run.sh documents macOS Keychain shadowing and deletion as operationally required, but the brief explicitly states that applicability to T3's Agent SDK path is unmeasured; T3's ClaudeHome.ts provides per-instance config isolation.
claims.test: On macOS, create two isolated T3 Claude instances with distinct injected credentials and a deliberately conflicting Keychain login, run identical authenticated probes, and compare init.account identity and server-side account telemetry with and without Keychain removal.

claims.claim: THEORY: T3 should not delete a user's global Keychain credential as part of its broker integration.
claims.evidence: aigate-run.sh's clear_shadow_login deletes the developer's stored Claude credential, while T3 is an embedded multi-provider application that must coexist with ordinary Claude Code use.
claims.test: Run brokered T3, standalone Claude Code, and simultaneous sessions on one Mac; confirm that brokered requests use the selected account, standalone requests retain their login, and no credential is rewritten or deleted outside the broker's isolated configuration scope.

claims.claim: THEORY: Model discovery should initially be a T3-side, versioned route-profile contract rather than a new aigate model endpoint.
claims.evidence: aigate has no model endpoint; Muse requires a specific base URL, bearer auth, model and tier mappings, context limit, and tool-name workaround, while Kimi requires a separate Anthropic-compatible route and auth family.
claims.test: Implement route profiles for native Claude, Muse, and Kimi and verify that each produces a valid model catalog entry, correct environment, successful probe, correct context limit, and no cross-route credential leakage; compare maintenance cost against a server-provided /api/models endpoint.

claims.claim: VERIFIED: Muse cannot safely be treated as only a model-name substitution because its route requires distinct authentication and runtime settings.
claims.evidence: aigate-muse.sh behavior in the brief: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.meta.ai, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN unset, all Claude model-tier variables mapped, CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS=1007997, and a dedicated settings file for the 64-character tool-name limit.

claims.claim: THEORY: Account exhaustion should be handled first at session boundaries, with explicit reverse states such as selecting, active, parked, exhausted, reauth-required, and broker-unavailable; automatic mid-session hopping is a later capability.
claims.evidence: aigate already models parking, usage refresh, and reauth_needed; T3 is event-sourced and must represent reversible provider/session state rather than hiding a relaunch in a shell process.
claims.test: Define contract events and replay them through server, web, desktop, and mobile clients; simulate selection failure, limit parking, reauthentication, cancellation, and broker outage, then verify deterministic projection and reversible UI state.

claims.claim: THEORY: The smallest maintainable implementation is an optional generic broker interface with an aigate adapter, not hardcoded aigate calls inside ClaudeAdapter.
claims.evidence: AGENTS.md requires optional, generic, remote-ready integrations; T3 already has provider-instance environment and secret seams; hardcoding a LAN URL or vendor-specific logic would violate that architecture.
claims.test: Implement a no-op broker plus an aigate implementation selected by configuration, then run the full provider matrix with the broker disabled and confirm byte-for-byte equivalent behavior for existing configurations.

claims.claim: VERIFIED: There is no evidence in the supplied repository facts that Codex, Cursor, Grok, or OpenCode currently have an aigate-compatible account-rotation contract.
claims.evidence: The brief identifies aigate's current selector as Claude-specific, reports the GPT rung retired, and supplies no account-broker implementation for those adapters.

claims.claim: THEORY: Provider decisions for v1 should be Claude=opt-in broker and route profiles; Codex=unchanged/no aigate rotation; Cursor=unchanged/no support; Grok=unchanged/no support; OpenCode=unchanged/no support.
claims.evidence: Only Claude account selection and the Muse/Kimi Claude-binary routes are evidenced; Codex plan rotation is explicitly unknown and the GPT path is reported retired.
claims.test: For each adapter, document auth inputs, process boundary, model discovery, quota signal, and safe retry semantics; promote a provider only after an account-specific integration test demonstrates all five.

claims.claim: THEORY: The ordered implementation should be: (1) Monday spike for Agent SDK credential precedence and isolated config, (2) add generic broker configuration and contracts, (3) implement aigate selection/telemetry with fail-closed behavior, (4) add Claude route profiles for native Claude/Muse/Kimi, (5) add session-boundary retry and reverse-state events, (6) wire all clients and documentation, and (7) submit only a small generic upstream PR while keeping the aigate adapter external if maintainers reject it.
claims.evidence: This sequencing follows the load-bearing unknown in Claude credential precedence, existing T3 seams in ProviderInstanceEnvironment.ts and ClaudeHome.ts, and the stated upstream constraint that large features are likely to be closed.
claims.test: Complete each phase with an integration test and replay test; specifically require that disabling the broker restores current behavior, aigate outage does not expose secrets or silently select the wrong account, and web/desktop/mobile render every broker state.

claims.claim: UNMEASURED: The exact T3 event names, client stores, and UI components required to expose broker states across web, desktop, and mobile cannot be identified from the supplied brief alone.
claims.evidence: The brief identifies the event-sourced architecture and contracts location but does not provide client file paths or existing provider-status event schemas.
claims.test: Trace one existing provider lifecycle command from packages/contracts through server decider/projector and each client, then record the exact files and add broker states beside that established path.

challenges.their_claim: The existing aigate-run.sh behavior can serve as the model for first-class T3 integration.
challenges.problem: A shell wrapper owns process relaunch, Keychain deletion, output classification, and --continue semantics, whereas T3 uses the Agent SDK and event-sourced session management; assuming equivalence risks silently authenticating the wrong account or duplicating tool effects.
challenges.test: Execute the credential-precedence and session-resume experiments described above against the actual T3 ClaudeDriver and Agent SDK.

challenges.their_claim: Aigate's existing APIs are sufficient for account brokering and model support.
challenges.problem: They are sufficient for Claude account selection and usage reporting but not for model enumeration; Muse and Kimi also require route-specific settings that cannot be represented by an account token alone.
challenges.test: Define and validate a T3 route-profile schema; if centrally managed model discovery is required, prototype and measure a versioned aigate /api/models contract.

challenges.their_claim: Automatic account hopping is a success criterion for the integration.
challenges.problem: The requirement does not establish that hopping is safe within an Agent SDK session, especially after tool calls or partial streamed responses; session-boundary hopping is safer but may not satisfy uninterrupted continuation.
challenges.test: Use fault injection after text, tool-call, and tool-result phases and verify exactly-once observable tool behavior when resuming on another account.

needs_research: Whether Claude Agent SDK credential precedence on macOS consults or rewrites the global Keychain despite CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.
Whether Agent SDK sessions can resume on a different OAuth account without invalidating context or duplicating side effects.
The exact T3 web, desktop, and mobile client file paths and existing provider-status contracts.
Whether T3's current Claude probe exposes reliable quota or rate-limit signals before a turn fails.
Whether Kimi K3 has a stable official endpoint, authentication contract, and redistribution policy suitable for a generic T3 route profile.
Whether upstream maintainers would accept a small generic broker-contract PR despite the stated contribution posture.
members.dissent: I cannot yet agree to per-turn or mid-thread account hopping, Keychain deletion, or an aigate model-listing endpoint as part of v1. The credential-precedence, session-resume, and client-contract experiments must pass first; until then, ship optional session-boundary Claude brokering with T3-side route profiles and explicit no-support decisions for the other providers.

members.position: We recommend a two-phase architecture: Phase 1 (zero-diff) maps aigate setup tokens and alternative endpoints (Muse/Kimi) into distinct T3 Provider Instances using existing `ProviderInstanceEnvironment` variables and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` isolation. Phase 2 introduces an upstreamable lightweight `CredentialBroker` interface in `apps/server/src/provider/` that dynamically invokes aigate's `/api/select` and `/api/events/limit` endpoints on session init and retry, bypassing macOS Keychain conflicts by enforcing per-instance sandbox homes. Other providers (Codex, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode) are explicitly excluded from account rotation in v1 as aigate holds no active multi-account rotators for them.

claims.evidence: apps/server/src/provider/ProviderInstanceEnvironment.ts:3-16 (`mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment`) and apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts:128

members.dissent: Cannot mark consensus ready until the macOS Keychain isolation test under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR with @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk is verified empirically.

implementation_plan.smallest_shippable_step: Define separate T3 Provider Instances (e.g., 'Claude - Bastardtech', 'Claude - Personal', 'Meta Muse') in ~/.t3/userdata/settings.json, populated with aigate tokens via a local helper CLI, utilizing T3's existing mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment behavior.

provider_decisions.claude: First-class integration via aigate /api/select token broker and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR isolation.
provider_decisions.codex: Single credential only (out of scope for rotation; GPT rotator retired).

architecture.model_catalog: Extend CLAUDE_MODEL_CATALOG in apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeProvider.ts with optional custom model definitions for Meta Muse (muse-spark-1.2-contributor) and Kimi K3.
architecture.turn_and_session_hopping: Catch 429/quota errors at ClaudeAdapter.ts query turn boundary, call aigate POST /api/events/limit, re-fetch account from GET /api/select, and re-issue turn with refreshed CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.

members.position: Stop designing the cathedral. The load-bearing hazard (does Keychain/stored login outrank CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN under Agent SDK + per-instance CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR?) is UNMEASURED, and until that experiment runs every integration sketch is fanfic. Use T3's already-native multi-instance primitive as three dumb Claude instances whose env secrets an external aigate side-car refreshes — zero broker concept in T3 core, zero upstream PR theater, Claude-only v1. Model listing for muse/kimi is T3-side static route config, not aigate's job; aigate has no models API and pretending otherwise invents scope.

challenges.their_claim: Design the integration plan for T3 Code to use aigate as first-class account selector + model listing
challenges.problem: Assumes in-process brokering and aigate-served model lists are the goal. aigate has no models API; T3 already has multi-instance; the SDK keychain hazard is unmeasured. First-class broker is the largest, least upstreamable surface.
challenges.test: Run Keychain/SDK experiment first. If per-instance CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR isolates creds, implement external side-car that only writes instance secrets + optional exclude/select — measure LOC in T3 vs shim. If isolation fails, shim/wrapper on pathToClaudeCodeExecutable is the only honest path.

challenges.their_claim: Model listing including muse/kimi should be part of the aigate integration design
challenges.problem: Conflates credential vault with model catalog. aigate stores keys and Claude account headroom; muse model ids, context token ceilings, tool-name limits, and tier env mapping are client knowledge (aigate-muse.sh). Pushing /api/models into aigate invents an endpoint to avoid a static catalog entry in ClaudeProvider.
challenges.test: Add muse/kimi as static alternate routes / pseudo-models in T3 catalog gated by optional env; no aigate change. If product needs dynamic discovery, then and only then add aigate /api/models — until a consumer fails without it, do not build it.

challenges.their_claim: Per-turn headroom pick + hop when dry is the integration shape
challenges.problem: aigate selects per process launch; T3 threads are long-lived. Per-turn select without proving mid-session hop doubles API chatter and still needs out-of-headroom detection on the T3 side (SDK errors vs aigate poll). Best-headroom at session start + park-on-limit event is the existing proven loop — per-turn is an unasked upgrade.
challenges.test: Instrument one long thread: select once at session start; on rate-limit classification POST /api/events/limit and either fail the turn with reselect guidance or resume-hop. Compare failure rate vs per-turn select latency and wrong-account rate.

members.dissent: I will not agree to a first-class in-server 'credential broker' abstraction, aigate-specific URLs in contracts, or an aigate /api/models dependency until (1) the SDK credential-shadow experiment is run and logged, and (2) a side-car-or-shim design that only uses existing ProviderInstanceEnvironment + multi-instance is shown insufficient. Monday morning ship: the macOS/Linux credential isolation experiment + a 1-page decision (shim vs secret-writer side-car vs in-tree broker) with file touchpoints — not code that calls aigate.

members.position: T3 Code should integrate aigate as a credential broker via env injection at the existing `mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment` point, plus a new `aigateProvider` property on the instance config that auto-populates `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `AIGATE_ACCOUNT`, and optionally `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. The integration must be (a) optional — aigate is off by default, (b) generic — the broker URL and token come from `~/.t3/userdata/secrets/aigate.json`, not hardcoded, (c) minimal — touch < 5 files in the server (ClaudeProvider, ClaudeDriver, ClaudeAdapter, ProviderConfig, contracts). Model listing for non-Anthropic models like Muse/Kimi is out of scope for v1: those are "provider instances with custom env" today (user creates a Claude instance named "muse" with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` override), not a T3-or-aigate problem. The Monday-shippable step: `claudeProvider` supports a `useAigate: boolean` + `aigateHost` field; on instantiation, if true, call `GET /api/select?host=...` and inject the returned token+account into the per-instance env, otherwise behave exactly as before.

claims.claim: aigate-run.sh's keychain-delete trick (macOS) bypasses a stored Claude login that otherwise outranks injected CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. If T3 uses the Agent SDK with per-instance CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (separate from ~/.claude/), this shadowing may not apply — but it is UNMEASURED and the experiment is: start two T3 provider instances, one with aigate token injected, another with a stored login in its custom CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; verify which token the SDK's query() actually uses by examining the Authorization header on an intercepted request.
claims.evidence: Chair's cross-cutting hazard: aigate-run.sh documents that on macOS the claude binary rewrites the Keychain entry ~1s after launch and stored login beats env injection. The Agent SDK path T3 uses may create a separate credential store per CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (analysis of SDK source would settle this with a config-dir corruption test). No experiment has been run yet.
claims.test: Set up a test T3 instance with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/t3test, inject AIGATE_ACCOUNT=test via env, run a probe query, intercept outgoing request headers at the network level. If Authorization matches AIGATE_ACCOUNT's token, shadowing is avoided. If it matches the developer's stored login, shadowing applies even to per-instance config dirs.

claims.claim: aigate has no model-listing endpoint and no model-aware selection logic. It stores provider keys (65 providers) but never enumerates or filters by model.
claims.evidence: Chair's repo inspection: aigate/src/server.js lines 295-298 `pickRanked` selects by headroom only; `src/providers.js` is a key catalog, no models. `GET /api/capabilities` returns key counts and selectable-account counts but no models. Git log confirms no models table ever added.

claims.claim: T3 Code's existing `mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment` and `ServerSecretStore` can inject arbitrary env vars per provider instance, including CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and AIGATE_ACCOUNT, without modifying the Claude SDK query() call site.
claims.evidence: Chair-verified: `ProviderInstanceEnvironment.ts:3-16` overlays per-instance vars, `packages/contracts/src/providerInstance.ts:104-113` defines `ProviderInstanceEnvironmentVariable` with `sensitive` flag, `serverSettings.ts:316-376` shows secrets stored in `~/.t3/userdata/secrets/*.bin`. A test already exercises `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` through this path. `Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts:128` calls mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment before spawning the SDK.

claims.claim: The `aigate-run.sh` retry/park/rotate logic (up to 3 attempts on headless, account parking via POST /api/events/limit, re-select with exclude=) is unnecessary for T3's integration because T3 manages retries at the turn level and can probe headroom via /api/accounts rather than parsing stderr. However, the 'interactive supervision' feature (re-launch with --continue on a new account) does not map to T3's architecture where sessions span many turns via stream-json, not process restarts.
claims.evidence: Chair reading of aigate-run.sh: retry loop is for headless `-p` mode; interactive supervision checks usage on exit and relaunches the claude binary with --continue. T3 uses `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` `query()` which is a streaming API call, not a process lifecycle. The --continue mechanism is not used by T3. Source: T3's ClaudeAdapter.ts passes options to query(), no --continue flag observed.

claims.claim: Codex/Cursor/Grok/OpenCode account rotation is out of scope for v1. Only Claude provider instances will support the aigate broker, because aigate's primary select/accounts/events APIs are Claude-specific (token type sk-ant-oat…, Anthropic rate-limit headers, Anthropic account introspection).
claims.evidence: Chair's aigate API inspection: /api/select returns `setup_token` (sk-ant-oat…), /api/accounts rate-limit fields are `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-{5h,7d}`, /api/events/limit and /api/events/usage are Anthropic-account-aware. aigate has keys for other providers (OpenAI, Grok, etc.) but no select/accounts/limit posture for them. The gpt rung is retired (aigate-gpt.sh 402s, retired 2026-08-04 per chair).

claims.claim: The cross-machine state conflict (keychain clearing on Mac when T3 desktop and ai CLI share a box) is a real concern: aigate-run.sh deletes the developer's real Claude login. If T3 desktop app on the same Mac also relies on stored login (for its non-aigate Claude instance), the two mechanisms conflict. Mitigation: T3's aigate integration must use per-instance CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (already done) to isolate its credential store from the system ~/.claude, avoiding the keychain altogether.
claims.evidence: The conflict is documented in aigate-run.sh ('Shadow-login clear'). T3 already sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR per instance (ClaudeHome.ts:27-33). The theory that this isolates the credential store is plausible but unverified: the SDK may fall back to Keychain regardless of CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Test: run a T3 instance with custom CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env; if the SDK creates its own credentials file in that dir and uses it, isolation works. If it still reads the system Keychain, it doesn't.
claims.test: Run T3 with a custom empty CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, no auth env vars; if SDK creates .credentials.json inside that dir, isolation works. If it attempts to read system keychain and fails, isolation incomplete.

claims.claim: Muse/Kimi models can be supported in T3 today as custom Claude provider instances with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` overrides, without any aigate integration. The `aigate-muse.sh` env-injection pattern is exactly what T3's `mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment` does natively.
claims.evidence: Chair's aigate-muse.sh analysis: sets `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.meta.ai`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<LLM|key>`, maps models via env vars. This is identical to T3's per-instance env injection mechanism. No special T3 code needed — user creates a provider instance with those env vars. T3's ClaudeAdapter already respects ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN (they are passed through mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment).

challenges.their_claim: The integration plan should include model listing for non-Anthropic models (Muse, Kimi K3) as a first-class feature.
challenges.problem: aigate has no model-listing endpoint. Adding one would require a new aigate endpoint that enumerates models from provider APIs (Meta, Kimi) — significant work on the aigate side with no clear contract for what 'listing models' means across providers. Meanwhile, T3 users can manually configure Muse/Kimi as Claude instances today via env overrides, with model names set per-instance. The model listing ask conflates credential brokering with model discovery, which are separable concerns. The Monday smallest shippable step does not need this.
challenges.test: Remove the model-listing requirement from v1 scope; validate by confirming that a user can set up a 'muse' Claude instance in T3 with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and have it work for a turn.

challenges.their_claim: The integration should support account rotation mid-session (hop accounts when headroom runs dry during a conversation).
challenges.problem: aigate-run.sh rotates between processes, restarting claude with --continue. T3 sessions are long-lived streaming API calls — restarting the process would lose the stream state. T3's architecture does not support mid-turn account switch. The 'park and re-select' pattern only makes sense between T3 turns (when the next turn can be routed to a new provider instance with a different account). T3 already supports this: create multiple Claude provider instances (e.g. claude_bastardtech, claude_personal), and the session can be continued on a different instance between turns. But aigate's automated 'out of headroom → re-select → relaunch' is not isomorphic to T3's turn-by-turn instance switching. This needs a different pattern (see position: probe headroom before each turn via /api/accounts, skip an instance if its account is low).
challenges.test: Prove T3 can switch provider instances between turns by building a test where turn 1 goes to claude_bastardtech, turn 2 (manually configured) goes to claude_personal, and the conversation history is preserved via the session manager.

needs_research: Does the Agent SDK's query() respect CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN even when a valid Keychain login exists under a different CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR? Experimental cross-check with intercepted headers.

members.position: Build it fork-first as a generic, opt-in 'credential broker' resolved at claude-subprocess spawn time: for broker-enabled instances the server calls an external selector (aigate /api/select, or any endpoint/command returning an env overlay) and merges the result into the child env, with the broker token stored through the existing sensitive ProviderInstanceEnvironment / ServerSecretStore machinery. Alt-endpoint models (Muse, Kimi K3) ship as T3-side static pseudo-model instances of the claude provider — the brief's option (a) — because aigate verifiably has no models endpoint and the route parameters are hand-tuned facts, not enumerable data. Headroom management ports the warden's two mechanisms into the server: proactive exclusion from /api/accounts before spawn, and reactive parking via /api/events/limit when typed 429/quota errors surface, with parked/reauth-needed projected into contracts for all clients. Per-provider decisions: Claude supported in v1; Codex, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode explicitly unsupported (aigate holds no account pools for them; the gpt rung is retired). But no integration code ships until two zero-code checks land: E0, whether the env seam is per-child or a process.env mutation, and E1, whether a stored login outranks injected env under the Agent SDK with per-instance CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR — if it does, the per-spawn design needs a shadow-login strategy before anything else. Monday morning: read the 14 lines of ProviderInstanceEnvironment.ts and run E1 using probeClaudeCapabilities' init.account.email/tokenSource as the identity readout — half a day, no diffs.
